text: Stellantis books a €22.2B ($26B) charge tied to a business reset after overestimating the speed of the energy transition. Shares drop about 25-27% across Europe and the U.S. The company suspends its 2026 dividend and plans up to €5B in hybrid bond issuance while targeting only mid-single-digital revenue growth and low-single-digit margin gains for 2026. Management signals a slower, demand-governed electrification path and exits its 49% stake in the NextStar battery JV.

meta.note: Tension between the writedown and claimed return to positive volume growth in H2 2025.

text: Amazon falls about 9% as its $200B 2026 capex plan crystallizes broader investor fear of an AI overbuild. The six largest tech firms shed more than $1T in market value over the week as Q4 capex totals (~$120B) imply 2026 spending that could exceed $660B. Selling spreads from cloud leaders to AI hardware suppliers, while market reactions diverge across firms despite similar investment trajectories.

meta.note: Hard to separate valuation repricing from short-term positioning effects.

text: Bitcoin jumps about 10% intraday back above $70,000 after briefly trading below $61,000 the prior day, moving in tandem with a broad risk-asset rally (Dow +1.9%, S&P +1.4%, Nasdaq +1.5%). Price remains roughly 45% below its October high, with elevated volatility and mixed positioning between dip-buyers and forced sellers.

meta.note: Short-term stabilization coexists with unresolved downside risk.

text: President Trump's Truth Social post containing a video with racist imagery of former President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama depicted as apes is deleted after bipartisan backlash. Trump states he "condemns" the racist parts but will not apologize and claims he did not see the segment before it was posted, blaming a staffer. Criticism comes from both Republican and Democrat lawmakers calling the imagery offensive.

meta.note: The addition of a refusal to apologize introduces intra-government authority conflict without changing the core structural geometry.

text: Once Upon a Farm prices its IPO at $18 and opens at $21, rising about 20% in its NYSE debut under ticker OFRM. The offering raises roughly $198M and values the company at about $724M. Sales grew to $156.8M in 2024 (+66% YoY) even as losses widened, as retailers expand shelf space for organic, less-processed children's foods.

meta.note: Tension between rapid revenue growth and deepening losses.
